title: Alms in secret
summary: Jesus teaches the people to give alms privately rather than to seek public praise.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus teaches that alms should not be done before people for their attention.
He warns against sounding a trumpet in synagogues and streets to gain glory from people.
He teaches giving alms in secret.

unspecified_visual_details: Whether alms or a trumpet are shown

spoken_dialogue.text: Verily, verily, I say that I would that ye should do alms unto the poor;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

narration.text: That thine alms may be in secret;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The trumpet and public giving are teaching examples, not narrated events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an actual alms-giving event or trumpet-sounding as occurring.

title: Prayer in secret
summary: Jesus contrasts public prayer for attention with entering a private room to pray.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus teaches against praying publicly in synagogues and street corners to be seen.
He teaches entering a closet, shutting the door, and praying in secret.

unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of a synagogue, street corner, or closet

spoken_dialogue.text: But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

narration.text: pray to thy Father who is in secret;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Public and private prayer are examples within the teaching; the text does not narrate either happening.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a separate person praying in a closet or public place.

title: How to pray
summary: Jesus teaches against vain repetitions and says the Father knows what people need before they ask.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus warns against vain repetitions in prayer.
He says the Father knows what people need before they ask.

unspecified_visual_details: Any visual representation of prayer or divine knowledge

spoken_dialogue.text: Be not ye therefore like unto them,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

narration.text: your Father knoweth what things ye have need of

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The text does not describe a visible divine appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict vain repetition as a present event.

title: The prayer
summary: Jesus gives a model prayer addressing the Father and asking for forgiveness and deliverance from evil.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus instructs his listeners to pray after this manner and recites the prayer.

unspecified_visual_details: The physical posture of Jesus or the listeners

spoken_dialogue.text: Our Father who art in heaven,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

spoken_dialogue.text: Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

spoken_dialogue.text: And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

spoken_dialogue.text: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

spoken_dialogue.text: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, forever. Amen.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The quoted prayer is presented as teaching, not as a separate prayer event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Father as visibly appearing.

title: Forgiveness
summary: Jesus teaches that forgiving others and receiving forgiveness are connected.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus teaches that the Father will forgive those who forgive others.
He teaches that those who do not forgive others will not be forgiven by the Father.

spoken_dialogue.text: For, if ye forgive men their trespasses
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

narration.text: neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage states a principle; it does not narrate an act of forgiveness.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent people or a particular trespass.

title: Fasting in secret
summary: Jesus teaches against displaying a sad face to show fasting and instructs listeners to wash and anoint themselves instead.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus warns against disfiguring one's face to appear to people to be fasting.
He instructs a person who fasts to anoint their head and wash their face.
He teaches that fasting should be seen by the Father in secret.

spoken_dialogue.text: But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thy head, and wash thy face;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

narration.text: That thou appear not unto men to fast,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The examples describe how to fast; no fasting person is narrated as present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a separate person fasting or washing as an event.

title: Treasures
summary: Jesus teaches not to store earthly treasure but to lay up treasure in heaven, where one's heart will be also.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus warns against storing treasures on earth, where moth, rust, or thieves can destroy or take them.
He teaches storing treasures in heaven, where they cannot be corrupted or stolen.
He says the heart will be where the treasure is.

unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of earthly or heavenly treasure

spoken_dialogue.text: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

narration.text: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage uses treasure as a teaching image; it does not narrate a treasure scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal heavenly treasure store or thieves breaking in.

title: The eye and the light
summary: Jesus uses the eye, light, and darkness as figures in his teaching.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus says that if the eye is single, the whole body will be full of light.
He says that if the eye is evil, the whole body will be full of darkness.

unspecified_visual_details: Any visual metaphor for light or darkness

spoken_dialogue.text: The light of the body is the eye;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

narration.text: thy whole body shall be full of darkness.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Light and darkness are figures of speech in the teaching, not literal visible transformations.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a person literally glowing or becoming engulfed in darkness.

title: Two masters
summary: Jesus teaches that a person cannot serve both God and Mammon.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus teaches that a person cannot serve two masters and cannot serve God and Mammon.

spoken_dialogue.text: Ye cannot serve God and Mammon.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The two masters are part of a teaching comparison.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Mammon as a visible character.

title: Jesus addresses the twelve
summary: After speaking to the people, Jesus looks upon the twelve he chose and tells them they are chosen to minister; he begins teaching them not to worry about food or clothing.

explicit_facts.text: After speaking, Jesus looks upon the twelve he chose and speaks to them.
He tells the twelve they are chosen to minister to the people.
He tells them not to worry about life, food, drink, or clothing.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus and the twelve are together while he addresses them.
unspecified_visual_details: The twelve disciples' individual identities and appearance

spoken_dialogue.text: Remember the words which I have spoken.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

spoken_dialogue.text: ye are they whom I have chosen to minister unto this people.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The focus shifts from teaching the people to addressing the twelve.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the disciples' names or distinguishing appearances.

title: The fowls of the air
summary: A speaker describes fowls that do not sow, reap, or gather into barns, says the heavenly Father feeds them, and asks two questions.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says fowls do not sow, reap, or gather into barns, yet the heavenly Father feeds them.
The speaker asks whether the listeners are better than the fowls.
The speaker asks who can add one cubit to their stature by taking thought.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold the fowls of the air, for they sow not, neither do they reap nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

spoken_dialogue.text: Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The fowls are discussed as part of a teaching; the verses do not place them visibly in the setting.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the speaker or listeners from outside these verses.
Do not require visible birds or depict a visible divine figure.
Do not depict anyone physically growing by a cubit.

title: Lilies of the field
summary: Jesus tells the twelve to consider lilies and grass, teaching that God clothes the field and will clothe them.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus tells the twelve to consider lilies of the field, which grow without toil or spinning.
He says Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of the lilies.
He teaches that God clothes the grass of the field and will clothe the listeners if they are not of little faith.

unspecified_visual_details: Whether lilies or grass are visible
The disciples' individual identities and appearance

spoken_dialogue.text: Consider the lilies of the field how they grow;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

narration.text: they toil not, neither do they spin;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Solomon is mentioned in a comparison, not described as present.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Solomon or turn the comparison into a narrated historical scene.

title: Seek first the kingdom
summary: Jesus tells the twelve not to worry about necessities, to seek God's kingdom first, and not to worry about tomorrow.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus tells the twelve not to worry about what to eat, drink, or wear.
He says the heavenly Father knows they need these things.
He teaches them to seek first God's kingdom and righteousness, and says these necessities will be added.
He tells them not to worry about tomorrow.

unspecified_visual_details: The disciples' individual identities and appearance
Any visual representation of the kingdom or tomorrow

spoken_dialogue.text: But seek ye first the kingdom of God and his righteousness,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

narration.text: Take therefore no thought for the morrow,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The scene concludes Jesus' teaching on worry and provision.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict imagined worries or future events as present scenes.
